content:
jordan: Quick heads-up — p95 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate jumped ~200ms after yesterday's routing-policy rollout. p50 unchanged, p99 flat. Not sure why the middle percentile moved. Screenshot: https://redwood.internal/s/abc123 :eyes:

maria_obs: Interesting. do we have the route breakdown enabled for that panel? Could be a weighting change across model variants.

sam_platform: I pulled raw samples from the metrics store and my first guess is sample-origin mix changed. p95 can move if a mid-tail cohort gained weight. Did the fallback weight change on the rollout?

jordan: We moved to the new fallback policy (region-aware fallback) yesterday at 03:00 UTC. The rollout was 100% for EU, 50% for NA (by weight). I expect it to affect p99 if heavy tails were hit, but p99 didn't budge.

lee_metrics: We might be seeing an artifact in percentile attribution. Our dashboard computes p50/p95/p99 via a rollup pipeline that merges per-route t-digests. If a request is routed to a fallback that preserves original route tag *and* also emits a "fallback_observed" sample to the fallback route, we could be double-counting the same logical request across two cohorts, causing an apparent shift in intermediate percentiles.

emily: That rings true. I noticed earlier some telemetry rows with both `route=primary` and `route=fallback` for same request_id. Example: ``request_id=abc, route=primary, latency=45; request_id=abc, route=fallback, latency=245`` — downstream merge treats them as independent samples.

jordan: Ugh. So what are the options?

sam_platform: Two short-term fixes: 1) stop emitting fallback samples when primary is preserved (easy, but loses visibility of fallbacks). 2) add a provenance tag that marks samples as `origin=route-of-execution` and `dedupe_hint=request_id` and teach the rollup to prefer executed-route samples when `dedupe_hint` is present. I'd prefer (2) since it keeps visibility and allows correct rollups.

maria_obs: We already have `request_id` in telemetry but it's optional in some clients. Making it required for server-side emitted fallback samples is doable. Rollup change will need metadata: `sample_origin=executed|intended|dup` and perhaps `fallback_reason=capacity|latency|region`.

lee_metrics: Implementation notes: the rollup ingestion window must be updated to dedupe by `(dedupe_hint, window)` and pick the sample with `origin=executed` if present, otherwise fall back to `intended`. Also add a dashboard toggle to surface "sample provenance" so PMs can inspect composition. Query sketch (pseudo-SQL):
```sql
SELECT
  percentile(50, latency) as p50,
  percentile(95, latency) as p95,
  percentile(99, latency) as p99,
  sample_origin
FROM metrics
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND time > now() - 2h
GROUP BY sample_origin
```

emily: Can we do a short-lived backfill to verify whether deduping fixes the spike before coding the rollup? e.g., run an offline aggregator over last 48h with dedupe logic and compare p95.

sam_platform: Yes. I can run a backfill job on the parquet dumps — will take ~30m for 48h at current cluster load. If p95 moves back down in the backfill, we're confident it's the telemetry duplication.

jordan: Sounds good. Priority: high. This p95 change is tripping a slack alert for a customer-facing SLO. Please post results.

devops-bot: Backfill job queued: job_id=bf-452111-01, owner=sam_platform, estimated_time=35m

lee_metrics: UX ask for Console: once we have `sample_origin` in rollups, add a small provenance chip on the tooltip (e.g., "origin: executed | intended | deduped") and a legend filter so users can hide intended-only samples.

maria_obs: I'll open a tiny RFC for the telemetry field additions: `sample_origin`, `fallback_reason`, and make `request_id` recommended for server-side telemetry. Linking RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/percentile-provenance

emily: After backfill, if dedupe explains >80% of the p95 delta, we should hotfix the rollup to dedupe in ingestion path and ship the Console tooltip change in the same sprint.

jordan: Thanks all — @sam_platform please drop updates and a quick before/after chart in this thread once the backfill finishes. Also ping me if you need guardrails to avoid changing billing metrics during the test.

sam_platform: Will do. starting now.

(15m later)

sam_platform: Backfill done. Results: offline dedupe lowers p95 for /v1/generate from 420ms -> 210ms in the 00:00-06:00 UTC window where rollout weight changed. p50/p99 unchanged. Draft artifact: https://redwood.internal/bf/452111-01/chart.png

jordan: Nice. That matches hypothesis.

maria_obs: RFC updated with backfill results and proposed ingestion dedupe. Requesting review from eng-platform and eng-sre.

lee_metrics: I'll add the Console tooltip mock and a small feature flag for provenance display so we can toggle while we validate with customers.

emily: I'll coordinate a short note to support so they don't get noisy alerts during rollouts once we deploy the dedupe.

jordan: Great work team. Follow-up actions assigned: sam -> prod hotfix for ingestion dedupe (traceable by job id), maria -> telemetry RFC final + required request_id for fallback emissions, lee -> console provenance chip PR, emily -> support comms. Closing the thread after actions are live. :tada:
